numberItems.stem: Air pressure is leaking down while you drive. The tractor protection valve will close automatically when pressure falls into what range?
options: Only when the tanks are completely empty
numberItems.explanation: The tractor protection valve closes automatically when air pressure is low, in the range of 20 to 45 psi (p. 6-5). Some websites say 25–40 psi.

numberItems.stem: On a newer tractor you **push in** the red 8-sided knob. What happens?
options: The trailer emergency brakes come on
The tractor parking brakes are set
Air is supplied to the trailer
numberItems.explanation: The red 8-sided trailer air supply knob is pushed in to supply the trailer with air and pulled out to shut the air off and put on the trailer emergency brakes (p. 6-5).

numberItems.stem: On an older vehicle, the trailer air supply control may be a lever. What are its two positions?
numberItems.explanation: Older lever-type controls have a "normal" position for pulling a trailer and an "emergency" position to shut off the air and put on the trailer emergency brakes (p. 6-5).

numberItems.stem: In a newer air-brake vehicle, what does the **yellow, diamond-shaped** knob control?
numberItems.explanation: The yellow diamond-shaped push-pull knob controls the parking (spring) brakes (p. 5-4); the red 8-sided knob is the trailer air supply (p. 6-5).

numberItems.stem: How many air lines run between each unit of a combination vehicle?
options: 2 — the service line and the emergency line
numberItems.explanation: Every combination vehicle has 2 air lines, the service line and the emergency line, running between each vehicle (p. 6-5). "Control line" is just another name for the service line.

numberItems.stem: When coupling, which color is used to mark the **service** line glad hands?
numberItems.explanation: Blue is used for the service lines and red for the emergency (supply) lines (p. 6-6).

numberItems.stem: The **emergency** air line is also called the:
numberItems.explanation: The emergency line is also called the supply line; control line and signal line are other names for the service line (p. 6-5).

numberItems.stem: When you connect glad hands, how should the two couplers be held as you press the seals together?
options: Lined up straight, end to end
At a 90-degree angle to each other
numberItems.explanation: Press the two seals together with the couplers at a 90-degree angle to each other, then turn the glad hand to join and lock them (p. 6-6).

numberItems.stem: Your trailer air tanks have automatic drains. How often should you still open the drain valves?
options: Never — automatic drains do the job
Only when the brakes feel weak
numberItems.explanation: Drain each tank every day; automatic drains keep most moisture out, but you should still open the drains to make sure (p. 6-6).

numberItems.stem: You are pulling doubles. Where should the shut-off valves be **closed**?
options: Only at the back of the last trailer
Nowhere — all shut-off valves must be open
At the back of the first trailer
numberItems.explanation: All shut-off valves must be open except the ones at the back of the last trailer, which must be closed (p. 6-7).

numberItems.stem: Which units are **not** required to have spring brakes?
options: Any trailer pulled as part of a double
Converter dollies and trailers built before 1975
numberItems.explanation: Converter dollies and trailers built before 1975 are not required to have spring brakes (p. 6-7). March 1, 1998 is the trailer ABS date.

numberItems.stem: Trailers and converter dollies are required to have ABS if they were built on or after:
options: ABS is never required on trailers
numberItems.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to have ABS (p. 6-8).

numberItems.stem: During your walk-around you look for the trailer's ABS malfunction lamp. What color is it?
numberItems.explanation: Trailers have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner (p. 6-8).

numberItems.stem: An older trailer has no ABS lamp. How can you tell if it has ABS?
options: Look under it for the ECU and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes
See whether it has a red 8-sided knob
See whether it has blue and red glad hands
numberItems.explanation: For units made before the required date, look under the vehicle for the ECU and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes (p. 6-8).
